newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservative chairman defends aide quitting.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservative chairman defends aide quitting.

text.p: British Conservative Party chairman Brian Mawhinney said party colleague James Cran had resigned as a parliamentary private secretary because he was keen to concentrate on fighting for his marginal seat in the next election.

His resignation as aide to Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Patrick Mayhew was confirmed on the eve of the Conservative Party's crucial last party conference before the election, which must be staged by next May.
The unpaid post of parliamentary private secretary is seen as the first step on the ladder to ministerial responsibility.
Mawhinney told BBC Television that Cran, a prominent member of the so-called Eurosceptic wing of the party, had resigned his post three weeks ago.
"Boundary changes meant he had a lot more work to do in his constituency," Mawhinney said. "There is a danger of over-estimating these things ... It is not a matter of significance."
